content_rules.voice: Very simple, easy English. Short sentences. Common everyday words. No idioms. Friendly and warm, but plain.
content_rules.answer_length: About 120 words maximum. Short paragraphs with a blank line between them.
content_rules.no_tier_names_or_allowances: No plan includes a free call. Every call is paid. Do not quote the price here — it is shown when the team confirms, and it moves with the plans.
content_rules.flow: The flow is: the founder requests a slot from the team's real availability, the team confirms it, and payment follows confirmation through Razorpay. Never describe a request as a booking, and never promise a call is arranged before the team has said yes.

walk_log.rebuilt: This group was written against the old flow and then the flow was rebuilt, because the old one could not work: no plan includes a free call, so the entitlement gate refused every founder with a 402, and there was no way to pay past it. Discovery calls were unbookable by anyone. Requesting is now free, the team confirms, and payment follows.
observed: Slots are the team's real availability: weekday times filtered against the host calendar's busy blocks, so a time that is offered is a time somebody can actually take.
Requesting a slot creates a PENDING request. Nothing is charged and no calendar event is created.
The team confirms from the admin queue. That is when the meeting is made and the founder emailed.
Founders can now cancel and reschedule their own calls. Rescheduling a request keeps it a request; rescheduling a confirmed call makes a new meeting.
Requests are ordered for the team by priority first, then soonest slot — a request for Tuesday is answered before one for next month, whoever asked first.

answers.question: What happens on a discovery call, and who am I talking to?
answers.answer:
It is 30 minutes with someone from our team, not a bot.

You pick a time that suits you, and the team confirms it. Once they do, your call appears under "Your calls" on the Discovery call page with a Join button, and you also get an email with the time and the link.

The useful version of the call is you bringing something specific: your report, a decision you are stuck on, or a finding you disagree with. Say what you want to cover when you request it, and they will come prepared.

It is a conversation, not a presentation.

answers.question: Is the discovery call free? Why can't I book one?
answers.answer:
It is not free. A discovery call costs Rs 300 for 30 minutes, on every plan.

That is per call. No plan includes one, so nobody has an allowance to run out of.

Asking for a slot costs nothing, though. You pick a time and send the request, our team checks it against their diary and confirms, and payment comes after that -- once you know the call is actually happening.

If the button is not there at all, it is because discovery calls are not included on the free plan.

answers.question: How many calls do I get, and what does an extra one cost?
answers.answer:
As many as you like, and each one costs Rs 300.

There is no limit and no allowance. Book one call or book six -- every one is Rs 300 for 30 minutes, and it is the same price on every plan.

So there is no such thing as an extra call here. There is just the next call, at the same price as the last one.

You are only charged once the team has confirmed the time. Requesting a slot costs nothing.

answers.question: Do unused calls roll over?
answers.answer:
There is nothing to roll over. Calls are not an allowance.

No plan includes free calls, so there is no monthly quota to use or lose. Each call is requested and paid for on its own, at Rs 300 for 30 minutes.

Which means you are never missing out by not booking this month. Book one when you actually need one.

answers.question: Can I just talk to a person instead of doing all this?
answers.answer:
You can, and a discovery call is how.

It is worth knowing what you lose, though. Without the diagnosis, whoever you speak to is starting from scratch in 30 minutes, the same as any first meeting. With it, they already know how you work and what Ally found, and the call starts somewhere useful.

So if you have the time, do the diagnosis first and bring the report. If you do not, request a call anyway and say what is going on.

For anything shorter, message support and a person will reply.

answers.question: Is the call going to be a sales pitch?
answers.answer:
It is not meant to be, and if it turns into one we would want to know.

The point of the call is your situation — going through your report, a decision you are stuck on, or something you think Ally got wrong.

If paid help would genuinely suit what you describe, they may mention it. What should not happen is a call that becomes a pitch when you came with a problem.

If that is what you get, please tell us afterwards. It is the kind of thing we would want to correct rather than defend.

answers.question: How do I move or cancel a call I've booked?
answers.answer:
You can do both yourself, from your call in the app.

Cancel it if you no longer need it, or reschedule it to a different time — you do not have to email anyone. If the call was already confirmed, rescheduling creates the new meeting and sends you a fresh link. If it was still waiting on the team, it simply moves to the new time and stays with them.

Please change it as early as you can. The slot goes back for someone else, and the team plans their week around what is booked.

answers.finding: RESOLVED. Cancel and reschedule did not exist in the app or the API when this group was first written; a founder had to email support. Both are now built and tested. Rescheduling preserves whether the call was a request or a confirmed booking, so a moved request does not silently become a booking.
